intent: Attach stackable, chained semantics to each Java corpus program: source, surface summary, functional relation, operational story, verification obligations, and a Strata Core sketch target. The corpus currently has 50 buildable Java programs.

semantic_chain.consumes: Java source file, class name, method names, signatures, comments, and simple control-flow shape.
semantic_chain.emits: A concise surface summary for each method.
semantic_chain.obligation: The surface summary must describe the method in terms that are checkable against the source.

semantic_chain.consumes: The surface summary and the method signature.
semantic_chain.emits: A mathematical input/output relation that ignores incidental Java execution details.
semantic_chain.obligation: The functional relation must make the informal intent precise enough to become a postcondition.

semantic_chain.consumes: The functional relation and the Java body.
semantic_chain.emits: A bounded execution story for calls, conditionals, loops, array accesses, string traversals, and mutation.
semantic_chain.obligation: The operational story must explain why the Java steps implement the functional relation.

semantic_chain.emits: Preconditions, postconditions, loop invariants, frame conditions, and proof obligations.
semantic_chain.obligation: The verification layer must expose the proof points needed to connect execution to the functional relation.

semantic_chain.emits: A Strata Core/Boogie-like procedure name and contract target.
semantic_chain.obligation: The Strata Core sketch must preserve the verification condition as a named procedure/spec target.

programs.program_semantics: Pure integer helper methods. The interesting stack relation is that direct Java arithmetic and method calls collapse to simple integer formulas.

layers.surface: Compute the product of two integers.
layers.functional: result = a * b.
layers.operational: Single return step; no heap reads or writes.
layers.verification: Postcondition result == a * b.

layers.surface: Compute the sum of two integers.
layers.functional: result = a + b.
layers.operational: Single return step; no heap reads or writes.
layers.verification: Postcondition result == a + b.

layers.surface: Multiply by base exponent times.
layers.functional: For exponent >= 0, result = base raised to exponent.
layers.operational: A bounded for loop from 0 to exponent updates result := result * base.
layers.verification: Loop invariant after i iterations: result = base^i and 0 <= i <= exponent.

methods.name: maxOfThree
methods.signature: int maxOfThree(int a, int b, int c)

layers.surface: Return the largest of three integers.
layers.functional: result is one of a, b, c and every input is <= result.
layers.operational: Two conditional updates maintain best as the largest value seen so far.
layers.verification: Postconditions a <= result, b <= result, c <= result, and result == a || result == b || result == c.

methods.name: score
methods.signature: int score(int a, int b, int c)

layers.surface: Compose sum, product, and maxOfThree into one score.
layers.functional: result = ((a + b) * c) + max(a, b, c).
layers.operational: Calls sum, product, maxOfThree, then sum again.
layers.verification: Relational postcondition connects caller result to callee summaries.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for universal positivity check. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Check that every item is positive.
layers.functional: Result is true iff all entries are greater than zero.
layers.operational: A bounded loop clears ok when it finds a nonpositive value.
layers.verification: Invariant: ok implies every scanned value is positive.

layers.surface: Return length when all values are positive.
layers.functional: Result is items.length iff allPositive(items), otherwise zero.
layers.operational: Branches on allPositive.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses allPositive summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for existential negativity check. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Check whether any item is negative.
layers.functional: Result is true iff at least one entry is less than zero.
layers.operational: A bounded loop sets found when it sees a negative value.
layers.verification: Invariant: found is equivalent to a negative in the scanned prefix.

layers.surface: Return a penalty when a negative exists.
layers.functional: Result is -1 iff anyNegative(items), otherwise zero.
layers.operational: Branches on anyNegative.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses anyNegative summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for clamping values to an inclusive interval. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

methods.name: clampValue
methods.signature: int clampValue(int value, int low, int high)

layers.surface: Limit a value to an interval.
layers.functional: Result is low, high, or value depending on bounds.
layers.operational: Two conditionals select the bounded result.
layers.verification: Postcondition: low <= result <= high when low <= high.

methods.name: clampAll
methods.signature: int[] clampAll(int[] items, int low, int high)

layers.surface: Clamp every array element.
layers.functional: result[i] = clampValue(items[i], low, high).
layers.operational: A bounded loop calls clampValue.
layers.verification: Invariant: output prefix is pointwise clamped.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for copying arrays without aliasing the input. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Return a same-length array with the same values.
layers.functional: For every index i, result[i] = items[i].
layers.operational: Allocates a new array and fills it with a bounded loop.
layers.verification: Invariant: copied prefix matches the input prefix.

layers.surface: Sum a copied array.
layers.functional: Result equals the sum of the original values.
layers.operational: Calls copy, then sums the copy.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses copy extensional equality.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for counting target occurrences. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Count target occurrences.
layers.functional: Result is the number of indices equal to target.
layers.operational: A bounded loop conditionally increments.
layers.verification: Invariant: count is target occurrences in the scanned prefix.

layers.surface: Check whether target appears once.
layers.functional: Result is true iff countTarget is one.
layers.operational: Calls countTarget and compares.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses countTarget summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for linear search for first index. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Find the first target index or -1.
layers.functional: Result is the least matching index, or -1 if none exists.
layers.operational: A bounded loop records the first match and preserves it.
layers.verification: Invariant: found is -1 or the first match in the scanned prefix.

layers.surface: Check membership using firstIndexOf.
layers.functional: Result is true iff firstIndexOf returns a nonnegative index.
layers.operational: Calls firstIndexOf and compares.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses firstIndexOf summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for interleaving two equal-length arrays. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Alternate values from two arrays.
layers.functional: result[2*i] = left[i] and result[2*i+1] = right[i].
layers.operational: A bounded loop writes two output slots per input index.
layers.verification: Invariant: output prefix contains interleaved pairs for scanned indices.

layers.surface: Return the length of the interleaved output.
layers.functional: Result is 2 * left.length.
layers.operational: Calls interleave and reads length.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses interleave length summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for checking nondecreasing array order. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Check nondecreasing order.
layers.functional: Result is true iff adjacent pairs are ordered.
layers.operational: A bounded loop compares each adjacent pair.
layers.verification: Invariant: sorted means every scanned adjacent pair is ordered.

layers.surface: Score an array based on sortedness.
layers.functional: Result is length for sorted input and negative length otherwise.
layers.operational: Branches on isSorted.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses isSorted summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for linear search for last index. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Find the last target index or -1.
layers.functional: Result is the greatest matching index, or -1 if none exists.
layers.operational: A bounded loop overwrites found at every match.
layers.verification: Invariant: found is the last match in the scanned prefix.

layers.surface: Compute the gap between first and last target occurrence.
layers.functional: Result is lastIndexOf(items,target) - firstIndexOf(items,target).
layers.operational: Calls firstIndexOf and lastIndexOf.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses both search summaries.

programs.program_semantics: Array scans that maintain extremum summaries.

layers.surface: Return the minimum item in a nonempty array.
layers.functional: result is an element of items and every array element is >= result.
layers.operational: A bounded loop updates best whenever a smaller value is found.
layers.verification: Invariant after i iterations: best is the minimum of items[0..i-1].

layers.surface: Return the maximum item in a nonempty array.
layers.functional: result is an element of items and every array element is <= result.
layers.operational: A bounded loop updates best whenever a larger value is found.
layers.verification: Invariant after i iterations: best is the maximum of items[0..i-1].

layers.surface: Return the spread between maximum and minimum.
layers.functional: result = max(items) - min(items).
layers.operational: Calls maxValue and minValue.
layers.verification: Caller postcondition follows from minValue and maxValue summaries.

layers.surface: Return the second largest value among exactly the first four items.
layers.functional: result is the largest value after removing one occurrence of the maximum from items[0..3].
layers.operational: Conditionally initializes largest/second, then scans two remaining elements.
layers.verification: Invariant: largest and second are the top two values among the prefix scanned.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for counting negative values in an array. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Test whether a number is negative.
layers.functional: Result is true iff value < 0.
layers.operational: Single comparison return.
layers.verification: Postcondition equates result with the comparison.

layers.surface: Count negative array values.
layers.functional: Result is the number of indices containing negative values.
layers.operational: A bounded loop calls isNegative and conditionally increments.
layers.verification: Invariant: count matches negatives in the scanned prefix.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for pairwise adjacent differences. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Return adjacent differences.
layers.functional: result[i] = items[i + 1] - items[i].
layers.operational: A bounded loop writes one adjacent difference per output index.
layers.verification: Invariant: output prefix contains correct adjacent differences.

layers.surface: Return the first adjacent difference.
layers.functional: Result is items[1] - items[0].
layers.operational: Calls differences then reads index zero.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses differences summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for counting positive values in an array. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Test whether a number is positive.
layers.functional: Result is true iff value > 0.
layers.operational: Single comparison return.
layers.verification: Postcondition equates result with the comparison.

layers.surface: Count positive array values.
layers.functional: Result is the number of indices containing positive values.
layers.operational: A bounded loop calls isPositive and conditionally increments.
layers.verification: Invariant: count matches positives in the scanned prefix.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for prefix sums over an integer array. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Return running totals.
layers.functional: result[i] equals the sum of items[0..i].
layers.operational: A bounded loop updates total then writes it.
layers.verification: Invariant: result prefix stores all completed running sums.

layers.surface: Return the last prefix sum.
layers.functional: For nonempty input, result is the sum of all items.
layers.operational: Calls prefixSums then reads the final element.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses prefixSums summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for bounded range sum over an integer array. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

methods.name: sumRange
methods.signature: int sumRange(int[] items, int start, int end)

layers.surface: Sum a half-open array range.
layers.functional: Result is the finite sum of items[start..end-1].
layers.operational: A bounded for loop accumulates one item per index.
layers.verification: Loop invariant: total is the sum of the scanned prefix.

layers.surface: Sum a whole array by delegating to sumRange.
layers.functional: Result is the finite sum of all array elements.
layers.operational: Calls sumRange with the full index range.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses the sumRange summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for copying with target replacement. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

methods.name: replace
methods.signature: int[] replace(int[] items, int target, int replacement)

layers.surface: Replace each target value in a copy.
layers.functional: Each output index is replacement when input equals target, otherwise the original value.
layers.operational: A bounded loop branches per element.
layers.verification: Invariant: output prefix follows the replacement relation.

methods.name: replacedCount
methods.signature: int replacedCount(int[] items, int target, int replacement)

layers.surface: Count replacement values after replacing.
layers.functional: Result counts replacement in replace(items,target,replacement).
layers.operational: Calls replace then countTarget.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses replace and countTarget summaries.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for reversing an array into a new output. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Return a reversed copy of the input.
layers.functional: For every index i, result[i] = items[length - i - 1].
layers.operational: A bounded loop writes mirrored indices.
layers.verification: Invariant: written output prefix equals the corresponding reversed input suffix.

layers.surface: Read the first item of the reversed copy.
layers.functional: For nonempty input, result is the last input element.
layers.operational: Calls reverseCopy then indexes zero.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses reverseCopy shape.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for left rotation of an integer array. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Move every element one position left and wrap the first value to the end.
layers.functional: For nonempty input, result[i] = items[i + 1] except the last result is items[0].
layers.operational: A bounded loop branches on the last index.
layers.verification: Invariant: output prefix follows the left-rotation relation.

layers.surface: Return the first value after a left rotation.
layers.functional: For length > 1, result is items[1].
layers.operational: Calls rotateLeftOne then reads index zero.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses rotateLeftOne shape.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for scaling every value in an array. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Multiply every array element by a factor.
layers.functional: For every index i, result[i] = items[i] * factor.
layers.operational: A bounded loop writes scaled values.
layers.verification: Invariant: output prefix equals scaled input prefix.

layers.surface: Sum the scaled array.
layers.functional: Result is factor times the sum of input values.
layers.operational: Calls scale then sums.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses scale element relation.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for weighted index sum over an integer array. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Multiply each value by its one-based index and sum.
layers.functional: Result is sum(items[i] * (i + 1)).
layers.operational: A bounded loop accumulates weighted terms.
layers.verification: Loop invariant: total is the weighted sum of the scanned prefix.

layers.surface: Compare two weighted sums.
layers.functional: Result is weightedSum(left) - weightedSum(right).
layers.operational: Calls weightedSum twice and subtracts.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses weightedSum summaries.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for counting zero values in an array. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Test whether a number is zero.
layers.functional: Result is true iff value == 0.
layers.operational: Single equality return.
layers.verification: Postcondition equates result with the comparison.

layers.surface: Count zero array values.
layers.functional: Result is the number of zero entries.
layers.operational: A bounded loop calls isZero and conditionally increments.
layers.verification: Invariant: count matches zero entries in the scanned prefix.

programs.program_semantics: Branch-heavy transition system with an explicit step fuel bound.

layers.surface: Compute the next Collatz value.
layers.functional: If n is even, result = n / 2; otherwise result = 3*n + 1.
layers.operational: One conditional branch based on n % 2.
layers.verification: Postcondition is a two-case branch on parity.

layers.surface: Run Collatz until one or until fuel is exhausted.
layers.functional: For maxSteps >= 0, result is the first k <= maxSteps such that iter(start, k) = 1, or maxSteps if none is reached earlier.
layers.operational: A bounded for loop checks value == 1 before each transition.
layers.verification: Invariant: after i iterations, value = iter(start, i) and steps = i unless an early return happened.

layers.surface: Return the Collatz value after bounded fuel or after reaching one.
layers.functional: For maxSteps >= 0, result = iter(start, k) where k is min(maxSteps, first step reaching one).
layers.operational: A bounded for loop updates value with nextNumber unless value is already one.
layers.verification: Invariant: current value is the iterated transition from start for the number of completed steps.

programs.program_semantics: Nested bounded loops compute distinct common values between two arrays.

methods.name: containsBefore
methods.signature: boolean containsBefore(int[] items, int limit, int target)

layers.surface: Check whether target appears before a limit.
layers.functional: result is true iff some index i with 0 <= i < limit has items[i] == target.
layers.operational: A bounded loop returns true on the first matching prefix element.
layers.verification: If false is returned, no scanned prefix element equals target.

layers.surface: Check whether target appears anywhere in the array.
layers.functional: result is true iff some valid array index contains target.
layers.operational: A bounded loop returns true on the first matching element.
layers.verification: Postcondition connects result to existential membership.

layers.surface: Count distinct values from left that also appear in right.
layers.functional: result is the cardinality of set(left) intersect set(right).
layers.operational: Scans left, tracks already-counted values in seen, and calls contains on right.
layers.verification: Invariant: seen[0..count-1] is duplicate-free and exactly the common values seen so far.

layers.surface: Return distinct common values in the order first seen in left.
layers.functional: Output contains each value in set(left) intersect set(right) exactly once, ordered by first occurrence in left.
layers.operational: Allocates countCommonDistinct length, then performs a second fill pass.
layers.verification: Invariant: result prefix is duplicate-free and complete for scanned left prefix.

programs.program_semantics: String traversal where each input character contributes two output characters.

layers.surface: Repeat every character twice.
layers.functional: For input length n, output length is 2*n and positions 2*i and 2*i+1 both equal text[i].
layers.operational: A bounded loop reads one character and appends it twice.
layers.verification: Invariant after i iterations: output length = 2*i and doubled positions are correct for prefix i.

layers.surface: Return the length of doubleUp(text).
layers.functional: For input length n >= 0, result = 2*n.
layers.operational: Calls doubleUp then reads the resulting length.
layers.verification: Caller postcondition follows from doubleUp length summary.

programs.program_semantics: Two-pass array filter: first count matching elements, then construct an output array.

layers.surface: Test divisibility by two.
layers.functional: result is true iff value mod 2 = 0.
layers.operational: Single return step using remainder.
layers.verification: Postcondition result == (value % 2 == 0).

layers.surface: Count even values in an array.
layers.functional: result equals the number of indices i where items[i] is even.
layers.operational: A bounded loop increments count only when isEven(items[i]) is true.
layers.verification: Invariant after i iterations: count equals the number of even values in items[0..i-1].

layers.surface: Return a new array containing exactly the even values in order.
layers.functional: Output length is countEvens(items), every output item is even, and order is inherited from input.
layers.operational: First pass allocates exact length, second pass writes matching values left to right.
layers.verification: Invariant: output prefix contains exactly the even values from the scanned input prefix.

layers.surface: Sum all integers in an array.
layers.functional: result is the finite sum of all array elements.
layers.operational: A bounded loop accumulates total += items[i].
layers.verification: Invariant after i iterations: total equals sum(items[0..i-1]).

programs.program_semantics: String indexing example. The first formal layer tracks reverse-index arithmetic and output shape.

layers.surface: Append each character followed by its reverse index.
layers.functional: For input length n, output is the concatenation of text[i] and decimal(n - i - 1) for i in 0..n-1.
layers.operational: A bounded loop reads charAt(i), computes reverseIndex, and appends both.
layers.verification: Invariant: after i iterations, output prefix encodes exactly input positions 0..i-1.

layers.surface: Sum the reverse indices for the input string.
layers.functional: For length n >= 0, result = n * (n - 1) / 2.
layers.operational: A bounded loop accumulates n - i - 1.
layers.verification: Loop invariant after i iterations: total = i * (2*n - i - 1) / 2.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for pointwise matrix addition. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Add two matrices pointwise.
layers.functional: result[row][col] = left[row][col] + right[row][col].
layers.operational: Nested bounded loops write pointwise sums.
layers.verification: Invariant: completed cells satisfy pointwise addition.

layers.surface: Read the top-left pointwise sum.
layers.functional: Result is left[0][0] + right[0][0].
layers.operational: Calls add then reads [0][0].
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses add summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for column sums of a rectangular matrix. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Compute one sum per matrix column.
layers.functional: result[col] is the finite sum of matrix rows at that column.
layers.operational: Nested bounded loops accumulate each column.
layers.verification: Outer invariant: completed columns have correct sums; inner invariant: total is current column prefix sum.

layers.surface: Return the first column sum.
layers.functional: Result is sum over matrix[row][0].
layers.operational: Calls columnSums then indexes zero.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses columnSums summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for maximum value in a matrix. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Find the maximum matrix value.
layers.functional: Result is an entry greater than or equal to every entry.
layers.operational: Nested bounded loops update best on larger values.
layers.verification: Invariant: best is the maximum over scanned cells.

layers.surface: Check whether the first cell is maximal.
layers.functional: Result is true iff matrix[0][0] equals max(matrix).
layers.operational: Calls max and compares.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses max summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for row sums of a rectangular matrix. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Compute one sum per matrix row.
layers.functional: result[row] is the finite sum of matrix[row].
layers.operational: Nested bounded loops accumulate each row.
layers.verification: Outer invariant: completed rows have correct sums; inner invariant: total is current row prefix sum.

layers.surface: Return the first row sum.
layers.functional: Result is sum(matrix[0]).
layers.operational: Calls rowSums then indexes zero.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses rowSums summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for trace of a square matrix. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Sum the diagonal entries.
layers.functional: Result is sum(matrix[i][i]).
layers.operational: A bounded loop reads diagonal cells.
layers.verification: Invariant: total is the diagonal sum for scanned rows.

layers.surface: Add matrix size to its trace.
layers.functional: Result is trace(matrix) + matrix.length.

layers.verification: Postcondition reuses trace summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for digit sum with bounded decimal places. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Sum up to six decimal digits.
layers.functional: Result is the sum of six low-order base-10 digits.
layers.operational: A fixed six-iteration loop extracts one digit per step.
layers.verification: Invariant: total is the sum of digits already extracted.

layers.surface: Check parity of the bounded digit sum.
layers.functional: Result is true iff digitSumUpToSix(value) is even.
layers.operational: Calls digitSumUpToSix and checks parity.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses digitSumUpToSix summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for counting positive divisors. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Count positive divisors up to n.
layers.functional: Result is the number of d in 1..n such that d divides n.
layers.operational: A bounded loop conditionally increments on divisibility.
layers.verification: Invariant: count is divisors in the scanned range.

layers.surface: Check whether exactly two divisors exist.
layers.functional: Result is true iff divisorCount(n) is two.
layers.operational: Calls divisorCount and compares.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses divisorCount summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for factorial by bounded multiplication. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Compute n factorial for nonnegative n.
layers.functional: Result is the product of integers 2..n.
layers.operational: A bounded for loop multiplies the accumulator.
layers.verification: Invariant after i: result is product 2..i-1.

layers.surface: Add one to factorial.
layers.functional: Result is factorial(n) + 1.
layers.operational: Calls factorial and adds one.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses factorial summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for iterative Fibonacci computation. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Compute the nth Fibonacci number iteratively.
layers.functional: For n >= 0, result is Fib(n).
layers.operational: A bounded loop advances previous/current state.
layers.verification: Invariant: previous = Fib(i) and current = Fib(i + 1).

layers.surface: Check parity of Fibonacci output.
layers.functional: Result is true iff fibonacci(n) is even.
layers.operational: Calls fibonacci and checks parity.
layers.verification: Postcondition reuses fibonacci summary.

programs.program_semantics: CS61B-style sample for greatest common divisor by bounded scan. The chain keeps source, surface intent, functional relation, operational loop/call story, verification obligation, and Strata target aligned.

layers.surface: Find the greatest common divisor by scanning candidates.
layers.functional: Result is the largest d <= min(a,b) dividing both inputs.
layers.operational: A bounded loop overwrites best on common divisors.
layers.verification: Invariant: best is the largest common divisor seen so far.

layers.surface: Check whether gcd is one.
layers.functional: Result is true iff gcdByScan(a,b) == 1.

programs.program_semantics: Small mutable disjoint-set structure. Current semantics is relation-level, with the parent array abstracted as a forest.

layers.surface: Find the representative root, returning -1 for invalid input.

layers.surface: Join two sets by size; do nothing for invalid or already-connected items.

layers.operational: Finds both roots, branches on invalid/same-root cases, then rewrites one root parent and one size slot.
layers.verification: Frame condition: only root metadata changes; relation after union is the equivalence closure adding left ~ right.

layers.surface: Construct a six-item union-find, union three edges, then return the component size if connected.
